Final Grade: A

Pretty good considering only scoring 73% in the final exam. The final exam allows single page double sided cheatsheet. The exercise and lab assignments are easy to get full marks as long as you pay attention to the lab instructions and course materials.
sections.workload: I guess the most difficult part might be the group project. Your team can choose from 3 topics and 1 of them is a fixed project that you can probably find sources and videos online. The hard part is to evaluate whether those sources are correct or not, so basically you have to do the project from start to finish. However, comparing to other courses in HKUST, 2 assignment and 1 group project report is already very generous imo.

sections.content: Basically everything you have to know if you are leading a project team. There are not too much fundamental sections if you just want to pass a test and get an OK grade, but if you would like to know more about project management, you can pretty much learn a lot.
sections.teaching: Between good and great, but not fabulous. He is the typical kind of nice professor you would imagine when you were imagining your university life in your high school years. It seems that he in person does have some project management experience, so you could learn from his experience  alongside the course material.
sections.grading:
A-range grades: 90 or above (31.4%)
B-range grades: 80 to 90 (54.3%)
C-range grades: 60 to 80 (14.3%)
Good grading, though it’s a pity for me. I would say a 31.4% A range is very generous. I got an overall score of 89.63, the highest score in our class who gets a B+. The syllabus is as follows:

Self-test reading assignments 20
Case analyses (2) 10
Lab assignments 20 (about MS project)
Final exam 50
sections.workload: Be ready for a heavy workload, packed up with two case studies (1000 words) , 6 lab projects, and 10 readings (each reading lasts for at least 2 hours).

sections.content:
Introducing the steps and procedures involved in managing different projects from start to the end. Also talked a bit on some advanced network diagrams (e.g. lag time, start to start relationship, finish to finish relationship etc). I think it's very interesting.
Also have 5 lab sessions to attend, make sure you wont skip the lab sessions though cuz u'll have to hand in assignment at the end (you'll get full marks if you have attended the session). MS project is quite a useful tool in project management.
sections.teaching:
Very organized and clear.
Make sure you'll answer his questions from time to time cuz he got participation cards, but I only get 3 cards at the end, my grades is still fine.
sections.grading:
Good grade!
I didn't skip any of his lessons (he'll take attendance randomly), the 50% final isn't difficult (with cheat sheet). Attending all his lectures will be fine, I got an A for this course at the end.
sections.workload:
Only one group project, I'll chose the Red Zuma project from Textbook that requires you to use MS Project.Only took 2 afternoons to finish.
In total of 2 assignments for the whole semester and the questions aren't difficult as long as you didn't skip any classes (he'll go through similar questions with you in class and teach you how to do it step by step)

sections.content: The course introduced project management in various aspects, points to note, concept like lag time and using software to better manage it. The software is very useful and I really learnt something in this course!
sections.teaching: I do enjoy Li, Qing's teaching style, very organized and easy to follow.
sections.grading: Quite good. Attending lectures and joting some notes will do. As far as I remember, the tests are not very difficult.
sections.workload: Not so sure about it as I took it last year. But it did not leave any bad impression in my mind, so should be fine :) Just remember there will be a project that you have to find a film to analyze how the people managed the project. Had a lot of fun!

sections.content: This course taught us concepts on project management, from the start to the finish of a project. There were 5 labs teaching us how to use the MS Project software which were quite useful.
sections.teaching: The professor was very helpful and the teaching was very clear. He encouraged participation in class and was not boring at all.
sections.grading: Grading was good. The project score will be given generously if you treat it seriously.
sections.workload: 2-3 assignments, 1 project and a final exam, not heavy compared to other courses. Assignments were easy and you can choose the topics for the project.

sections.content: The course is quite useful and related to the reality.   It teaches you how to use MS Project which I think seldom used by actual companies since companies usually have their own PM tool or just use Excel.
